arxiv-1503-05974.title: Hydrodynamic Limit for Spatially Structured Interacting Neurons
arxiv-1503-05974.creator: Aline Duarte, Guilherme Ost, Andrés A. Rodríguez
arxiv-1503-05974.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by Aline Duarte, Guilherme Ost, Andrés A. Rodríguez. We study the hydrodynamic limit of a stochastic system of neurons whose interactions are not of mean-field type and are produced by chemical and electrical synapses, and leak currents. The system consists of ε − 2 \varepsilon^{-2} neurons embedded in [ 0 , 1 ) 2 [0,1)^{2} , each spiking randomly according to a point process with rate depending on both its membrane potential and position.

arxiv-1807-10296.title: Robustness of Magic and Symmetries of the Stabiliser Polytope
arxiv-1807-10296.creator: Markus Heinrich, David Gross
arxiv-1807-10296.description: Abstract We give a new algorithm for computing the robustness of magic —a measure of the utility of quantum states as a computational resource. Our work is motivated by the magic state model of fault-tolerant quantum computation. In this model, all unitaries belong to the Clifford group.

arxiv-2202-13237.title: Orientation-Discriminative Feature Representation for Decentralized Pedestrian Tracking
arxiv-2202-13237.creator: Vikram Shree, Carlos Diaz-Ruiz, Chang Liu, Bharath Hariharan, Mark Campbell
arxiv-2202-13237.description: Abstract This paper focuses on the problem of decentralized pedestrian tracking using a sensor network. Traditional works on pedestrian tracking usually use a centralized framework, which becomes less practical for robotic applications due to limited communication bandwidth. Our paper proposes a communication-efficient, orientation-discriminative feature representation to characterize pedestrian appearance information, that can be shared among sensors.

arxiv-2303-09384.title: LLMSecEval: A Dataset of Natural Language Prompts for Security Evaluations
arxiv-2303-09384.creator: Catherine Tony, Markus Mutas, Nicolás E. Díaz Ferreyra, Riccardo Scandariato
arxiv-2303-09384.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) like Codex are powerful tools for performing code completion and code generation tasks as they are trained on billions of lines of code from publicly available sources. Moreover, these models are capable of generating code snippets from Natural Language (NL) descriptions by learning languages and programming practices from public GitHub repositories.

arxiv-2403-02027.title: Signature of localization-delocalization in collisional inhomogeneous spin-orbit coupled condensates
arxiv-2403-02027.creator: Swarup K. Sarkar, Rajamanickam Ravisankar, Tapan Mishra, Paulsamy Muruganandam, Pankaj Mishra
arxiv-2403-02027.description: Abstract We study the localization transition in spin-orbit (SO) coupled binary Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) with collisional inhomogeneous interaction trapped in a one-dimensional quasiperiodic potential. Our numerical analysis shows that the competition between the quasiperiodic disorder and inhomogeneous interaction leads to a localization-delocalization transition as the interaction strength is tuned from attractive to repulsive in nature.

arxiv-2406-18788.title: Wafer-Scale Fabrication of InGaP-on-Insulator for Nonlinear and Quantum Photonic Applications
arxiv-2406-18788.creator: Lillian Thiel, Joshua E. Castro, Trevor J. Steiner, Catherine L. Nguyen, Audrey Pechilis, Liao Duan, Nicholas Lewis, Garrett D. Cole, John E. Bowers, Galan Moody
arxiv-2406-18788.description: Abstract The development of manufacturable and scalable integrated nonlinear photonic materials is driving key technologies in diverse areas such as high-speed communications, signal processing, sensing, and quantum information. Here, we demonstrate a novel nonlinear platform—InGaP-on-insulator—optimized for visible-to-telecommunication wavelength χ ( 2 ) \chi^{\left(2\right)} nonlinear optical processes.

arxiv-2503-17529.title: Network-Driven Global Stability Analysis: SVIRS Epidemic Model
arxiv-2503-17529.creator: Madhab Barman, Nachiketa Mishra
arxiv-2503-17529.description: Abstract An epidemic Susceptible-Vaccinated-Infected-Removed-Susceptible (SVIRS) model is presented on a weighted-undirected network with graph Laplacian diffusion. Disease-free equilibrium always exists while the existence and uniqueness of endemic equilibrium have been shown. When the basic reproduction number is below unity, the disease-free equilibrium is asymptotically globally stable.

arxiv-2512-11446.title: YawDD+: Frame-level Annotations for Accurate Yawn Prediction
arxiv-2512-11446.creator: Ahmed Mujtaba, Gleb Radchenko, Marc Masana, Radu Prodan
arxiv-2512-11446.description: Abstract Driver fatigue remains a leading cause of road accidents, with 24% of crashes involving drowsy drivers. While yawning serves as an early behavioral indicator of fatigue, existing machine learning approaches face significant challenges due to video-annotated datasets that introduce systematic noise from coarse temporal annotations.

pmc-11389274.title: Mirror, mirror on my screen: Focus on self-presentation on social media is associated with perfectionism and disordered eating among adolescents. Results from the “LifeOnSoMe”-study
pmc-11389274.creator: Hilde Einarsdatter Danielsen, Turi Reiten Finserås, Amanda Iselin Olesen Andersen, Gunnhild Johnsen Hjetland, Vivian Woodfin, Jens Christoffer Skogen
pmc-11389274.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundSocial media use, perfectionism, and disordered eating have all increased over the last decades. Some studies indicate that there is a relationship between self-presentation behaviors and being exposed to others’ self-presentation on social media, and disordered eating. Studies also show that the relationship between focus on self-presentation and highly visual social media is stronger than for non-visual social media, hence facilitating upward social comparison.

pmc-11503447.title: Two Cases of Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP) Related to Viral Vector Vaccination ChAdOx1-S (AstraZeneca) and a Good Response after Thrombopoietin Receptor Agonist (TPO-RA) Therapy
pmc-11503447.creator: Konstantina Salveridou, Theodoros Tzamalis, Maika Klaiber-Hakimi, Sabine Haase, Stefanie Gröpper, Aristoteles Giagounidis, Claudio Cerchione, Drew Provan
pmc-11503447.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: In 2019, a new coronavirus disease emerged in Wuhan, China, known as SARS-CoV-2, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, and caused an ongoing pandemic. Symptomatology of the syndrome is variable, with complications extending to hematopoiesis and hemostasis. Approximately a year after onset of the virus, four vaccination formulas became available to the public, based on a viral vector or mRNA technology.

pmc-11711994.title: Predicting Mortality and Hospitalization in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction by Using Machine Learning
pmc-11711994.creator: Chieh-Yu Chang, Chun-Chi Chen, Ming-Lung Tsai, Ming-Jer Hsieh, Tien-Hsing Chen, Shao-Wei Chen, Shang-Hung Chang, Pao-Hsien Chu, I-Chang Hsieh, Ming-Shien Wen, Dong-Yi Chen
pmc-11711994.description: BackgroundFew studies have incorporated echocardiography and laboratory data to predict clinical outcomes in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).ObjectivesThis study aimed to use machine learning to find predictors of heart failure (HF) hospitalization and cardiovascular (CV) death in HFpEF.

pmc-12497604.title: The impact of physical activity and dietary habits on glycolipemic metabolism and inflammatory markers in the elderly: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12497604.creator: Wentao Zhang, Limin Zou, Jiangang Chen
pmc-12497604.description: ObjectiveMetabolic syndrome and chronic inflammation significantly impact the quality of life of the elderly. Physical activity and dietary habits are two of the most important modifiable aspects of lifestyle. Thus, this study investigated the effects of physical activity and dietary habits on relevant biomarkers in the elderly.MethodsA total of 2349 elderly participants aged 60–75 were recruited.

pmc-12574019.title: Haemoproteus syrnii and other haemosporidians infecting owls from North America
pmc-12574019.creator: M. Andreína Pacheco, Erica A. Miller, Josef Harl, Francisco C. Ferreira, Axl S. Cepeda, Gediminas Valkiūnas, Scott Beckerman, Mitchell Oswald, Nohra E. Mateus-Pinilla, Ananias A. Escalante
pmc-12574019.description: BackgroundHaemosporidians (Haemosporida, Apicomplexa), which include malaria parasites, are found in nearly all terrestrial ecosystems. Avian haemosporidians have been extensively studied; however, there is limited information on parasites in owls (order Strigiformes). Here, haemosporidians infecting North American owls were characterized using an integrative methodology.

pmc-12963697.title: Unphysical Structure Collapse in Quantum Mechanics Calculations With Continuum Solvation
pmc-12963697.creator: Andreas H Göller, Dieudonné T Tshitenge
pmc-12963697.description: The work reports on issues of the polarizable continuum solvent models conductor‐like polarizable continuum model (CPCM) and solvation model density (SMD) to adequately describe the relative conformer energies of drug‐like molecules that fit the quite common general structural pattern of two aromatic segments connected by a flexible linker.

Patients face challenges of a complexity of options, systemic access barriers, and need for support from healthcare providers (HCPs).

pmc-13594526.title: Life-history traits associated to West Nile virus seroprevalence in wild birds: Lessons from the recent outbreaks in Spain
pmc-13594526.creator: Ana Irina Martín-López, Josué Martínez-de la Puente, Sergio Magallanes, Jesús Veiga, Martina Ferraguti, Ramón Soriguer, Francisco Llorente, Pilar Aguilera-Sepúlveda, Miguel Ángel Jiménez-Clavero, Jordi Figuerola
pmc-13594526.description: West Nile virus (WNV) is a vector-borne zoonotic pathogen maintained in a bird–mosquito cycle, occasionally infecting humans and horses. It is considered a re-emerging pathogen in Europe, with recurrent outbreaks recently reported in Spain. However, the ecological and evolutionary factors driving spatio-temporal variation in WNV incidence remain unclear.
